clue.text: Bear with opinion we formed about article on hotel

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the article
the words opinion we are formed into a new shape, a rearrangement of their letters

parts.note: the definite article
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bear is put together from someone's opinion, with a grammatical article and a hotel tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Bear with' as 'put up with', but Bear is the definition; 'about' places the article inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A.A. Milne's honey-loving Pooh is the most famous fictional teddy, so this character name fits a bear.

clue.text: Those reporting to authorities corruption in football referees?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who expose wrongdoing to officials
second meaning, whimsical: referees literally blow whistles

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: football referees blow whistles to stop play, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Informants who expose wrongdoing within an organisation are called this, and the literal reading suits match officials using a whistle.

clue.text: Unusual number ready in Bulgaria for revolution

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation of number (No.)

indicators.note: revolution turns the currency round so it is read backwards in this down entry

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, and the lev is Bulgaria's currency

explanation.surface: A strange figure ready to start a revolution in Bulgaria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is British slang for money ('the readies'); Bulgaria's money is the lev, and 'for revolution' turns LEV into VEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something novel is new and strikingly different, a close synonym for unusual or original.

clue.text: Aussie vehicle seen underneath crashed lorries? That's doubtful

indicators.note: in a down entry the vehicle is placed beneath, after, the crashed letters
crashed lorries are wrecked, so the letters of lorries are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a ute is an Australian utility pickup truck

explanation.surface: An Australian pickup is seen under wrecked lorries, leaving an onlooker unsure what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: A ute is an Australian pickup truck; 'underneath' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irresolute is hesitant and undecided, so doubtful in the sense of wavering.

clue.text: Beat constable leaders overlooked for highest position in service, maybe

indicators.note: the leaders, initial letters, of the two words are ignored, overlooked

parts.note: a police beat is the street patrolled
a constable is a cop

explanation.surface: A beat constable is passed over for promotion to the top job in the police service.
explanation.walkthrough: STREET COP loses its leaders S and C, leaving TREET OP. The 'service' is the service tree, a European tree, not the police force the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The service tree is a species of tree, and its uppermost branches are the highest place in it.

clue.text: Yes, playing with cats will bring delight

indicators.note: playing with letters means toying with them to reorder them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that playing with cats will bring joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is intense joy or rapture, a stronger synonym for delight.

clue.text: Nothing to follow essentially cold current savoury dish

indicators.note: nothing comes last, following the other pieces
the essence, the central letters, of the word cold

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cold savoury dish is served, with nothing to follow it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially cold' gives OL, the middle of COLD; I for current comes next and O, 'Nothing', is 'to follow'.
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy stew of Spanish origin, so a hot savoury dish or medley.

clue.text: Shout from New Yorker also aboard ship

indicators.note: also goes aboard, inside, the shout

parts.note: holler is the American word for a shout
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A shout comes from a New Yorker who is also on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Yorker' just signals an Americanism; the shout is an American word for a yell.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries list a Hollander as a Dutch vessel as well as a native of Holland.

clue.text: Charlie stops Native American pocketing fantastic emerald, note the very best

indicators.note: the Cree pocket, hold inside them, the rearranged gem

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

indicators.note: Charlie stops up, plugs a gap within the rearranged gem
fantastic means fanciful, so the letters of emerald are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
me (mi) is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Native American holds a fantastic emerald, which is noted as the finest gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' makes MEDELAR from EMERALD, which C 'stops'; the Cree then pocket the lot and the note ME ends it. ME (or MI) is the third note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally cream of the cream, means the elite or the finest of all.

clue.text: French writer's visiting pianist occasionally in city

indicators.note: the writer's name visits, enters, the letters taken
occasionally takes every other letter of pianist

parts.note: taken as written
Jules Verne, the French novelist, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A French author's work is visited occasionally by a pianist in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of the pianist, and the French writer is Jules Verne.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is the main urban centre of the Scottish Highlands, granted city status in 2000.

clue.text: Time-waster is a little scoundrel, dithering around

indicators.note: the run is read around, the other way
only a little, a short run of letters, of the words is taken

parts.note: the letters run across these two words

explanation.surface: A dawdler is called a small-time rogue who keeps hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: The run RELDI, from scoundREL DIthering, read 'around' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a lazy person who fritters away hours, so a loafer who wastes time.

clue.text: Topless photos, there could be money in them

definitions.text: there could be money in them

indicators.note: the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: stills are photographs, especially from a film

explanation.surface: Topless pictures might earn their subjects money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests glamour photography; here it just removes the S from STILLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash registers in shops are drawers where takings are kept.

clue.text: Asian article of clothing, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, a word sounding like the tie

parts.note: a tie, worn round the neck

explanation.surface: An Asian item of dress, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, a country in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Ill-treatment in hospital wing

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
an arm is a wing or branch of an organisation or building

explanation.surface: Patients suffer abuse in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is damage or injury done to someone, which ill-treatment causes.

clue.text: Unit to measure heart's maintaining rhythm

indicators.note: the centre maintains, holds within it, the rhythm

parts.note: the heart is the centre; the 's stands for has, linking to maintaining
time is the rhythm or beat of music

explanation.surface: A unit measures how well a heart keeps its rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'heart's' as 'heart has': the centre has kept the rhythm within it. Time in music is its rhythm or metre.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a metric length, one hundredth of a metre, used for measuring.

clue.text: Student Frank extremely visible cycling in cloak

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from front to back

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
open means frank, candid

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of visible

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An outspoken student, highly conspicuous, rides a bike wearing a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: L + OPEN + VE gives LOPENVE; 'cycling' moves LOP from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap or enclose completely, as a cloak does, used as a verb.

clue.text: Triumphs in small Australian state over right-wingers

indicators.note: in a down entry the state sits over, above, the right-wingers

parts.note: Vic is short for Victoria, an Australian state
Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Conservatives win in a small Australian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' signals the shortening of Victoria to VIC; Tories are British Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Victories are wins or successes, a synonym for triumphs.

clue.text: Parted with profit day after store's closure

indicators.note: day comes after the store's last letter

parts.note: a yield is the return or profit from an investment

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the word store, whose closure is meant

explanation.surface: Someone surrendered a profit a day after their shop shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielded means gave up or handed over, so surrendered, parted with.

clue.text: Found old Conservative worried, being inspired by Liberal Democrat

indicators.note: to be inspired, breathed in, by the Lib Dem is to be inside it

parts.note: LD is the abbreviation for a Liberal Democrat
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: An old Tory, anxious, finds inspiration in a Liberal Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE is the past tense of eat in the sense of worry ('what's eating you?').
explanation.definitionFit: Located means discovered or tracked down, the past tense of found.

clue.text: Boy consumes new peeled fruit served up daily

indicators.note: served up in a down entry means read upwards, backwards
the boy consumes, takes inside himself, the other letters

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: peeled removes the skin, outer letters, of fruit

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy eats peeled fruit that is served to him every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips the outer letters of the word fruit itself, and 'served up' reverses everything in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal means happening every day or in the daytime, so recurring each day.

clue.text: Spontaneous individual assured of success

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a person born to do something, a sure thing

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the noun: someone with innate talent, as in 'she's a natural'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unaffected or instinctive; as a noun it is someone gifted who is bound to succeed.

clue.text: Posy of flowers, say, gone rotten

indicators.note: rotten letters have decayed out of order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A posy of flowers that has gone rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small bunch of fragrant blooms, a traditional name for a bouquet.

clue.text: Sound of perhaps husky female at rear of court

indicators.note: female goes at the rear, after court

parts.note: to woo is to court a lover

explanation.surface: A deep-voiced woman is heard at the back of a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' looks like a hoarse voice, but it is the sled dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Woof is the bark of a dog, and a husky is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Discover pair of smalls worn by American

indicators.note: the smalls are worn by, wrapped round, the American

parts.note: two S's, S being the abbreviation of small
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: Someone finds an American wearing two items of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' is British slang for underwear; here each 'small' is just the clothing size abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something out is British slang for figuring it out, so working out or discovering it.

clue.text: Heard cry from cat, unwell in garage, possibly

indicators.note: heard means the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: a cat's cry is a mew, and unwell is sick: mew sick said together

explanation.surface: A cat is heard crying, sick, in a garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garage' is not a car shelter but a genre of electronic dance music.
explanation.definitionFit: Garage is a style of dance music, an example of the art form, hence possibly.

clue.text: Time for wife during flood to make an impression

indicators.note: time stands for, replaces, wife

parts.note: to swamp is to flood

explanation.surface: A time for a wife to make her mark during a flood.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp is to imprint a mark by pressing down, as a seal leaves an impression.

clue.text: Food store distribution very neglected

indicators.note: very is neglected, left out

parts.note: delivery is the distribution of goods
taken as written

explanation.surface: A food shop's deliveries are badly neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods.

clue.text: Enhance stew with no end of lamb

indicators.note: with no means the letter is removed

parts.note: to braise is to stew slowly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so the last letter of lamb is the one dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook improves a stew by leaving out the end of the lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise is to lift or increase something, so to improve or boost it.

clue.text: Deny covering for this regularly absent broker in Wall Street?

indicators.note: deny covers, wraps round, the letters left

parts.note: to negate is to deny

indicators.note: letters of for this are absent at regular intervals, leaving the others

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Wall Street dealer, often away, denies cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of FOR THIS leaves OTI, which NEGATE covers. 'broker' is a verb here: to broker a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate is to arrange a deal by discussion, which is what brokering means.

clue.text: Relish vaguely unknown place to worship film star

indicators.note: vaguely means the letters of relish are imprecisely ordered, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Y is a mathematical unknown
a temple is a place of worship

explanation.surface: Fans vaguely enjoy an unknown shrine where they worship a movie idol.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirley Temple was a Hollywood child actress of the 1930s, a famous screen celebrity.
